explanation: England's top league. The one he'll happily cancel brunch plans for, every weekend from August to May.
The biggest tournament in the world. Once every four years it takes all the attention, from football and from him.
When the team doesn't let in any goals. Boring word, big deal.
Two goals in one match by the same player. A hat-trick is three.
Three goals in one match by the same player. Rare. He'll talk about it for weeks.
How many goals the stats nerds think a team should have scored based on chance quality. 'Should have scored more' has a number now.
Video Assistant Referee. The guys who pause the game to study replays. Source of half the world's football arguments.
When an attacker is past the last defender at the moment a pass is made. Goals get chalked off for this all the time.
Official warning. Get two in a match and you're sent off.
Sent off. Down to ten players. Usually a meltdown moment.
When a defender accidentally scores against his own team. Heartbreaking, hilarious, depending which side you're on.
Free shot from the spot, just the goalkeeper to beat. Awarded for fouls inside the box. Should be a goal almost every time.
Unobstructed kick awarded after a foul. The good ones bend around walls of defenders.
Set-piece from the corner flag when the defending team last touched the ball before it crossed their own goal line.
Sliding the ball between an opponent's legs. Maximum humiliation, minimum effort.
Kicking the ball before it touches the ground. Looks great when it works.
Scoring or passing with your head. Centre-backs make a career of these.
Plays up top, paid to score goals. The glory position.
Plays in the middle. Either creates the chances or stops the other team from creating them. Sometimes both.
Plays at the back. Stops the other team scoring. Underappreciated until they don't.
The one in the different shirt who gets to use his hands. Last line of defence.
Defender in the middle. Job: be tall, win headers, don't lose the striker.
Defender on the side. Modern ones spend half the match attacking.
Attacker who hugs the side of the pitch. Job: beat the full-back, deliver crosses, score from angles.
Team leader. Wears the armband. Talks to the ref so others don't have to.
Player who starts on the bench and comes on later. Up to 5 changes per match.
Where the substitutes sit. 'On the bench' means not in the starting eleven.
Finishing in the bottom three means dropping to the league below next season. Huge money implications.
Finishing high in a lower league means jumping up. Premier League promotion is worth roughly £170 million.
Two periods each season when clubs are allowed to buy and sell players. Summer is bigger than January.
Player goes to another club temporarily while still owned by his original team. Common for young players who need minutes.
Defended so heavily it looks like there's a literal bus across the goal. A compliment if you're the underdog, an insult otherwise.
Fast attack right after winning the ball back. Vulnerable defences hate this.
Chasing the opposition aggressively to force a mistake. The modern way to defend, popular with Klopp and Guardiola disciples.
Short, quick passing style. Barcelona made it famous. Either mesmerising or maddening, depending on your taste.
Europe's top club competition. Top four PL teams qualify. The midweek matches where the money is.
Europe's second-tier club competition. Slightly less glamour, still a Thursday-night staple for half the Premier League.
England's oldest cup. Knockout from January to May. Famous for upsets and tradition.
Match between two local rival clubs. Often nasty, always tense, never to be missed.
